{
  "correction_rules": [
    "Reduce forecast overshoots following sharp price spikes (e.g., after 72+ peaks) by 5–15% to avoid overcorrection.",
    "Adjust forecasts downward when sentiment history shows negative sentiment (e.g., -0.25 or 0.00) to reflect bearish momentum.",
    "Apply mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 2–5% to align with historical volatility.",
    "Increase downward bias in 3–5 day horizons when sentiment is neutral or negative, especially if true outcome shows downward drift.",
    "Avoid overreacting to recent highs: if model forecast is >10% above true outcome for 3 consecutive days, apply a 5–10% downward correction.",
    "For sentiment history with 0.50 or above, slightly increase downward bias to reflect cautious market behavior.",
    "In low-sentiment periods (all 0.00), allow model to follow historical mean but reduce volatility amplification by 10–20%."
  ]
}
